title: Paper Evidence Ledger — architectural claims to evidence mapping

claims.claim: stateHash and traceHash have distinct semantics: stateHash reflects authoritative world state; traceHash reflects history and changes only when history (events/provenance) changes.
claims.invariant: stateHash excludes event history and delivery state; traceHash includes history; eviction changes traceHash but never stateHash.
results: Deterministic replay produces identical hashes across 5+ runs (VER-2026-020)
Eviction changes traceHash, never stateHash (retention 51 tests)

claims.claim: Deterministic continuation: same seed + same intervention sequence + same tick schedule yields identical world state, hashes, RNG state, and causal decisions.
claims.invariant: Simulation is a pure function of (config, interventions, tick schedule); RNG lives in WorldState and is reconstructed on restore.
results: Identical stateHash across cadence configs A-H (P-016, 44 tests)
Replay hash ebaa28a3 identical across 5 runs (VER-2026-020)

claims.claim: Persistence and process-boundary restoration: a checkpoint survives process death and restores byte-identical authoritative state with deterministic continuation.
claims.invariant: Checkpoint serializes the full WorldState (incl. RNG register); restore + attachEngine resumes identically.
results: Restored world continues byte-identically vs uninterrupted (vertical-slice §3, temporal-boundary §7)

claims.claim: Branching, rewind, and convergence: timelines can fork and rewind; competing causal pressures converge deterministically; convergence never fabricates history.
claims.invariant: forkTimeline/rewindTo preserve lineage; convergence is deterministic; abandoned futures are handled at tick boundaries.

claims.claim: Provenance and attribution: every tracked quantity is attributable to its originating interventions via explain(), preserving multi-parent causes.
claims.invariant: provenance ring buffer with multi-parent nodes; provenanceRefs map quantity keys to nodes; explain() walks the ancestor graph.
results: Evicted attribution reported as truncated, not unexplained (attribution-windowing)

claims.claim: Event identity, ordering, and retention: events have stable identity, canonical delivery order (ascending streamSeq), and a bounded, explicitly-bounded retention window with detectable gaps.
claims.invariant: event id = f(timeline, tick, ordinal, content); delivery order = streamSeq; retention window [oldestRetainedSeq, highestEmittedSeq] with 3-state classifyCursor.
results: Ordering canonical and stable across eviction (retention)
claims.strength: SUPPORTED (retention value 500 is a policy, not validated optimum — VER-2026-025)

claims.claim: At-least-once delivery: consumers receive every retained fact at least once; duplicates are identifiable by stable event id and attempt counter.
claims.invariant: poll/ack with cursor semantics; DELIVERY_GUARANTEE = 'at-least-once'; attempt counter per event per channel.
results: Reconnect redelivers retained events, deduped by id (P-017)
Duplicate poll without ack cannot double-apply (temporal-boundary §8)

claims.claim: DeliveryState separation: delivery bookkeeping lives outside WorldState and never affects stateHash, traceHash, or simulation.
claims.invariant: DeliveryState is never hashed; slow/disconnected consumers cannot stall or change the world.
results: 200 CE ticks complete at <10ms/tick with un-acked consumer (P-017)
Slow consumer cannot pin unbounded history (retention)

claims.claim: Adapter/game authority boundary: game engines project CE state but never simulate causality; CE is the sole causal authority.
claims.invariant: Godot code contains zero causal rules and zero simulation RNG; adapter translates intents and projects state only.
results: Zero causal rules/RNG in all Godot slice code (grep-verified, P-018)
Adapter imports only public API surface (P-013)

claims.claim: Transport independence: HTTP and WebSocket transports deliver the same state/event semantics; transport never affects causality or hashes.
claims.invariant: Transport-neutral adapter contract; same poll/ack/stateSync/resync semantics over either transport.
results: In-process intervention 4.4x faster over WS (P-017 benchmark)
HTTP adequate at 5-20Hz; WS for push (P-017 decision)

claims.claim: Cross-platform determinism: identical seeds/interventions produce identical hashes on Windows (x64) and macOS (arm64).
claims.invariant: Simulation is platform-independent; no platform-specific float/order dependencies.
experiments: cross-platform-determinism.ts on Windows Node 22 and Mac mini Node 26 arm64
ws-boundary + vertical-slice + temporal-boundary suites run on both platforms
claims.strength: SUPPORTED (tested scenarios; not exhaustive over all configs)

claims.claim: Godot integration: CE deterministically drives a visible, interactive isometric game world with CE as sole causal authority.
claims.invariant: Godot renders/projects; adapter translates; CE simulates; the full causal chain is CE-originated.
experiments: GUI runs on physical Mac mini display (P-015/018) with screenshots iso_A..F
results: Bridge destroyed -> grain 10->13.13 -> hostility 0.1->0.62, all CE-originated (P-018)

overstrong_claims_audit.issue: Verified on 2 platforms for tested scenarios, not exhaustive over every config/seed
overstrong_claims_audit.precise_replacement: Cross-platform determinism holds for all tested scenarios (bridge + subsidy, seeds 42/43) on Windows x64 and macOS arm64; general claim requires the full suite cross-platform

overstrong_claims_audit.original_wording: Retention guarantee is precise: caught_up / deliverable / gap (supported) — but limit 500 implied as sufficient
overstrong_claims_audit.issue: EVENT_RETENTION_LIMIT=500 is a policy choice, not an evidence-validated optimum (VER-2026-025 explicitly flags this)
overstrong_claims_audit.precise_replacement: Retention semantics are precise and bounded at the configured limit; the limit value itself (500) is a policy parameter, not an evidence-backed optimum

overstrong_claims_audit.issue: Verified for the tested cadence matrix A-H and HTTP/WS/direct; not proven for arbitrary cadences
overstrong_claims_audit.precise_replacement: Determinism holds for the tested cadence configurations (A-H) and transports (HTTP/WS/direct); rendering/poll cadence is observational for these cases

non_claims: Exactly-once delivery is NOT claimed; only at-least-once with id-dedup
NOT a general-purpose game engine; single-world, single-town vertical slice only
No multi-town, combat, NPC AI, quests, procedural generation, multiplayer, or LLM integration
EVENT_RETENTION_LIMIT=500 is not claimed optimal; it is a bounded policy
No formal proof of determinism; determinism is empirically evidenced by reproducible hashes
WebSocket soak/lifecycle at production scale is NOT tested; only functional + failure-injection
No claim that provenance ring (4000) never evicts under unbounded runs; eviction is explicit and reported
No claim that the adapter is a complete game-engine integration SDK; it is a reference boundary
limitations: All 660 tests live under src/poc (integration-level); src/core/src/api have no unit tests
Cross-platform suite runs: full suite on Windows; WS/vertical-slice/temporal suites on macOS; not the entire suite on both
Performance numbers (P-010/012) are hardware-specific (Ryzen 3 4300U, Apple M4) and cadence-methodology-specific

tsc --noEmit has 7 pre-existing errors in P-011-era tool files (benchmark, headless, long-run, cross-platform-determinism, runtime-cadence, benchmark-investigation, runtime-boundary.test) — unrelated to the public API
P-010/P-011 have no dedicated doc files; evidence is in scripts + QMS records
Failure records document the design history (11 CE-relevant) — these strengthen rather than weaken claims, but must be disclosed
checkpoint chunking (P-018) is a transport-level fix with no dedicated WS-boundary test yet

freeze_recommendation.rationale: All 12 architectural claims are SUPPORTED by falsifiable tests + experiments + artifacts. 660/660 tests, tsc clean, retrace clean. The design history (11 failure records) shows invariants were discovered adversarially and hardened. No new causal features, transports, or optimizations were added in P-019.

frozen: Event identity formula (timeline, tick, ordinal, content)
adapter authority boundary (CE = sole causal authority)
requires_new_experiment: Any change to hashed state semantics (stateHash/traceHash inputs)
Any change to event identity or streamSeq ordering
Any change to intervention timing semantics
Adding a third transport (beyond HTTP/WS) that changes the adapter contract
Changing RNG or simulation math that alters hashes for existing scenarios
ordinary_implementation_allowed: Adding game content (regions, entities, interventions within existing schemas)
Adapter/scene code (Godot scenes, new UI, new input)
Transport server implementation details (chunking, buffering) that preserve semantics
Calibration of config parameters (thresholds, rates) without changing hashed semantics for the same config

freeze_recommendation.next_action: Write the research paper using this ledger as the evidence appendix. Any post-freeze architectural change must first produce a falsifiable experiment and updated ledger entry.
